source_class: NRL.com official Finals Week 1 team list and official NRL player profiles
rule: Raw profile facts are preserved separately from MAYHEM inference. Unpublished fields are FIELD_NOT_PUBLISHED. Derived trends identify genuine rounds used and do not establish causation.

players.trend_note: Rounds 25-26 show 47 and 51 minutes, 100 and 103 running metres, 34 and 27 tackles, and one then two missed tackles, with lock then interchange deployment. This is descriptive workload/role evidence only.
players.team_effect: Interchange/middle workload baseline enriched; no standalone confidence uplift assigned.

players.trend_note: Rounds 18-21 show movement from hooker to interchange, with minutes of 70, 33, 42 and 3 and running metres of 27, 53, 86 and 10. Role and workload variability are retained as uncertainty rather than a directional cause.
players.team_effect: Ball-playing middle/hooker utility baseline enriched; role variability retained as variance.

players.trend_note: Verified rounds 14, 15 and 27 show prop deployment throughout, minutes of 45, 44 and 52, running metres of 88, 77 and 109, and tackles of 25, 25 and 19. This indicates position continuity with variable production, without causal attribution.
players.team_effect: Prop continuity and middle-workload baseline enriched; no standalone confidence adjustment.

players.trend_note: All six 2026 NRL appearances are available: three 80-minute halfback games in Rounds 13-15, two 80-minute five-eighth games in Rounds 25-26, then 80 minutes at halfback in Round 27. Kicking metres rose from 88/146/193 early to 261/417/431 in the final three appearances. This is a genuine role/kicking-burden trend but remains LOW_SAMPLE_VARIANCE and does not establish causation.
players.team_effect: Reserve halves depth and verified kicking-burden trend enriched; low sample prevents directional uplift.
